lines: A 16-step trigger sequencer with a separate output for every step, where the gate, the repeat pattern, the probability and three modulation values are set one step at a time
Note — There is no run button. The sequencer starts and stops on triggers into RUN, and until one arrives it puts out nothing whatever the clock does; the RUN lamp shows the state.
Note — Click one of the sixteen step buttons to choose which step the GATE switch, the EACH switches, ELEN, PROB and the three MOD knobs along the bottom apply to.
Note — Those bottom controls always edit the chosen step and show its stored settings; on a freshly added module they read as off until a step button has been clicked once.
Sets how many steps are played before the sequence returns to its start, from 0 to 16
Sets how many times through the sequence before the sequencer stops itself, from 1 to 4; at 0 it runs until something stops it
Cycles the instrument name picture; nothing in the sequencer reads it, and the value saved with the patch is one behind the picture on screen, so a reloaded patch shows the one before
Chooses which step the GATE, EACH, ELEN, PROB and MOD controls along the bottom edit; choosing a step changes nothing about what the sequence plays
Turns the chosen step's trigger on or off; with it off the step produces nothing at its own output, at the GATE output or at the three MOD outputs
Turns the chosen step on for one position in its repeat cycle, so it plays on that pass through the sequence and is skipped on the others
Sets how many passes through the sequence the chosen step's repeat cycle runs over, from 0 to 5, which is how many of the five EACH switches are read
Sets the chance that the chosen step fires when its turn comes, from 0% to 100%, drawn afresh each time
Sets the value the chosen step sends to the MOD1 output, from -100 to 100, which reaches the jack as -10V to 10V; this knob moves continuously
Sets the value the chosen step sends to the MOD2 output, from -100 to 100, which reaches the jack as -10V to 10V; this knob steps in whole numbers
Sets the value the chosen step sends to the MOD3 output, from -100 to 100, which reaches the jack as -10V to 10V; this knob steps in whole numbers
Switches the sequencer between running and stopped on each rise past 0.5V; while REPEAT is set to anything but 0 and the sequence is already running, the rise is ignored
Moves the first step of the sequence, 0V giving step 1 and 5V giving step 16; the steps before the new start are left out of the loop
Advances the sequence by one step on each rise past 0.5V
Returns the sequence to its first step on a rise past 0.5V, and puts every step's repeat count back to the beginning of its cycle
Goes to 10V for one single sample when that step fires, and rests at 0V the whole of the rest of the time
Goes to 10V when a step fires and drops back to 0V as soon as the clock input falls below 0.5V, so it lasts as long as the high part of the clock
The MOD1 value of the last step that fired, a tenth of that step's knob setting in volts, held until the next step; a step that does not fire leaves 0V here
The MOD2 value of the last step that fired, a tenth of that step's knob setting in volts, held until the next step; a step that does not fire leaves 0V here
The MOD3 value of the last step that fired, a tenth of that step's knob setting in volts, held until the next step; a step that does not fire leaves 0V here
Menu — Disable all gates — turns the gate off on all sixteen steps at once
Menu — Generate random gate sequence (temp = 10) — sets each of the sixteen gates afresh, each with a one in ten chance of coming out on
Menu — Generate random gate sequence (temp = 25) — sets each of the sixteen gates afresh, each with a one in four chance of coming out on
Menu — Generate random gate sequence (temp = 50) — sets each of the sixteen gates afresh, each with an even chance of coming out on
Menu — Generate random gate sequence (temp = 75) — sets each of the sixteen gates afresh, each with a three in four chance of coming out on
Menu — Generate random gate sequence (temp = 90) — sets each of the sixteen gates afresh, each with a nine in ten chance of coming out on

HardSeqs.notes: Source read at commit 82b5d6f, the HEAD of https://github.com/regular-dev/hardseqs; its plugin.json is byte-for-byte the installed 2.0.0 manifest and there is no tag for the release. THE SIXTEEN PER-STEP OUTPUTS ARE ONE SAMPLE WIDE. clearAllStepOutputs() at HardSeqs.cpp:151 zeroes all sixteen on every process call, before the clock block at line 162 raises the one for the current step, so each is a single-sample 10V spike rather than a gate; the GATE output at line 178 is not cleared that way and instead follows the clock's high time. The three MOD outputs are cleared by nothing at all, so they hold the last fired step's value until the next clock edge. PARAM_IS_RUN and PARAM_SEL, indices 1 and 3 of the enum, are counted in the call to config() but never given a configParam or a widget, so they have no name, no tooltip and no position and cannot be clicked. The instrument label is parameter 31: HardSeqsWidget.cpp:84 sets it to the new frame number minus one, so the stored value trails the picture by one and a reloaded patch shows the previous name; nothing in process() reads it. The five EACH switches default to 0 in configParam (line 63) while StepEntry starts with all five true (HardSeqs.hpp:135), and setSelectedStep is not called from the constructor, so a newly added module shows them off while the steps behave as though they were on; clicking any step button brings the display into line. The random gate menu items change m_steps directly and do not refresh the GATE switch, so that switch can read stale until a step button is clicked. The bottom-row controls are attached with addChild rather than addParam, which keeps them out of ModuleWidget's parameter list but still leaves them clickable, and the census finds their positions. MOD1 has snapping turned off explicitly (HardSeqsWidget.cpp:178) while MOD2, MOD3, PROB and ELEN are snapping knobs. The probability draw uses std::mt19937 seeded from std::random_device, a fresh draw on each visit to the step. The README at the repository is short and describes POS as 0V for the first step and 5V for the sixteenth, which matches the code.
